name: The centurion of Capernaum
charge: Loving the nation and building the synagogue; not counting himself worthy that the Lord should come under his roof: speak the word only
summary: A Roman officer whose servant was dying sent the elders of the Jews, who pleaded that he was worthy, for he loved their nation and had built them a synagogue. He himself sent to say he was not worthy, and that a word would do, since he too was a man under authority. Christ marvelled, said he had not found so great faith in Israel, and the servant was healed in that hour.
offense: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed. For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth. The elders of the Jews besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this: for he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue. A Gentile who had done good to Israel and did not presume upon it.
judgment: When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.

entries.commentary: The centurion sends elders of the Jews to plead for him, and they say of him, He loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue. Say in a word, and my servant shall be healed. Christ marvelled and said, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

At Nain he meets a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she a widow. He had compassion on her and said, Weep not. Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. He that was dead sat up and began to speak, and he delivered him to his mother.

John's disciples ask, Art thou he that should come? and in that same hour he cured many, and answered by the works: the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist, but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he. The people and the publicans justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John; but the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.

They are like children in the marketplace calling one to another, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced. John came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and they said he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking, and they called him a gluttonous man. But wisdom is justified of all her children.

In the Pharisee's house a woman which was a sinner washes his feet with tears and wipes them with the hairs of her head, and the Pharisee reasons within himself that a prophet would have known what manner of woman she was. The parable of the two debtors answers him: he to whom most was forgiven loves most. Simon gave no water for his feet, no kiss, no oil for his head, and she had done all three. Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much. Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

The Most High called Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred, and from his father's house. He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go. Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
Abram departed at seventy and five years old, with Sarai and Lot, into the land of Canaan; Canaan is northeast Africa.
Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties.

The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Keep judgment and do justice, for His salvation is near to come and His righteousness to be revealed. Blessed is the man that does this and lays hold on it, that keeps the Sabbath from polluting it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.

The son of the stranger that has joined himself to the Most High is not to say the Lord has utterly separated him from His people, and the eunuch is not to say he is a dry tree. These strangers spoken of are Israel; the whole passage is the Most High speaking to Israel. To the eunuchs that keep His Sabbaths and take hold of His covenant, He gives a place and a name in His house better than of sons and daughters, an everlasting name that will not be cut off. The sons of the stranger that join themselves to Him, keep the Sabbath, and take hold of His covenant, He will bring to His holy mountain and make joyful in His house of prayer; their offerings will be accepted, for His house will be called a house of prayer for all people. The Lord God who gathers the outcasts of Israel says He will yet gather others to Him besides those already gathered.

All the beasts of the field and forest are called to devour. Judgment is turned on the failed leadership. The watchmen are blind and ignorant, dumb dogs that cannot bark, sleeping and loving to slumber. They are greedy dogs that never have enough, shepherds that cannot understand. They all look to their own way, every one for his gain, saying they will fetch wine and fill themselves with strong drink, and tomorrow will be as this day and much more abundant.

verses.text: And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.
Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.

Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant;

Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
